purpose: One/Zero interpretations bound to Step 1 v5 paycheck-date-only boundary controls and the Tax Year 2023 wage floor, with an explicitly pinned twelve-month matrix window.
source_basis: John Skowronski email 2026-07-30 with Min-Max and Pay Period 1/0 Summary Tables
Georgia JTC Step 1 Avg Wages and Hours Narrative
Georgia JTC Step 1 Avg Wages and Hours Diagram
GA JTC One Zero Methodology Overview.xlsx (SHA-256 C2F8CF527AF8423F88105D3EE77B30F938D7CFCE4E5D532A6C851F60701D310A)

OZ-01.decision: The twelve One/Zero month targets are pinned to August 2023 through July 2024. This window is configured explicitly rather than derived from BA-01 fiscal_year_begin, because the v5 fiscal window opens on 2023-07-28 and deriving month ends from it would shift the matrix to July 2023 through June 2024 and break alignment with John's summary tables.
OZ-01.falsified_by: John's Access run uses another matrix window.

OZ-02.decision: Min-Max coverage uses earliest included PPS through latest included PPE per employee, unit, and FEIN; assign 1 when Min PPS <= monthly cutoff <= Max PPE.
OZ-02.falsified_by: John's Access matrix uses paycheck dates or another range.

OZ-03.decision: Pay Period coverage uses PPS <= month target <= PPE. The Step 6 wording that requires PaycheckDate to be simultaneously <= and >= the last day of the month is treated as a source defect.

OZ-04.decision: For Month 12, when last PPE is in Month 12 and day > 15, use that PPE as target; otherwise use month end.
OZ-04.falsified_by: A later John-authored flow supersedes this rule.

OZ-05.decision: Pay Period One/Zero uses reviewed company cycle groups or practitioner-identified material payroll dates. The participation heuristic is diagnostic only and is not used to filter the v5 denominator.
OZ-05.falsified_by: John supplies a deterministic classifier validated against Access.

OZ-06.decision: No employee may contribute more than one count in a month. Flag every overlap; the reproducible provisional disposition is not sign-off authority. John's 2026-07-30 run deliberately left the twos unresolved so both sides can compare before that step.
OZ-06.falsified_by: John supplies an authoritative allocation rule or reviewed dispositions.

OZ-07.decision: Divide unit total by 12 and preserve unrounded, source-nearest-whole half-up, and application two-decimal views. One Zero Pay Periods.docx Step 7 requires nearest whole with .5 rounding up.
OZ-07.falsified_by: John uses another denominator or rounding sequence.

OZ-08.decision: Eligibility remains customer-wide; One/Zero grain includes employee, unit, and FEIN.
OZ-08.falsified_by: Access uses another entity allocation grain.

OZ-09.decision: Min-Max emits employee-unit-FEIN spans. Pay Period collapses employee-unit-FEIN-PPS-PPE rows before reviewed major-period selection.

open_questions_for_experian.november_zero_column: John's Min-Max summary reports 0 for M4 (November 2023) across all 101 units, and 54 of 101 Pay Period rows are also 0 in M4, while his average column still divides by 12. One Zero Pay Periods.docx Step 6 also specifies an Aug 2024 through Jul 2025 window that does not match this dataset, and cites an impossible date of 4/31/2025, which suggests day-31 month-target arithmetic.
open_questions_for_experian.employee_level_lists: Employee-level eligibility lists for both methods are required to close the residual sub-one-percent gap.

change_control.supersession_rule: Create a new version when Access or stakeholder evidence resolves an ambiguity; retain v5 with every run that used it.

resolved_on_2026_08_20_call.short_pay_period_numerator: Resolved. Numerator keeps all hours and wages; only the denominator is cleaned.
resolved_on_2026_08_20_call.pay_period_record_collapse: Resolved. John confirmed his run did not collapse multiple pay-code lines per pay period - 'I did not collapse the payroll... that's why I think my number was wrong.' Our collapse step is correct and his 659 is superseded.
resolved_on_2026_08_20_call.rounding_at_threshold: Resolved in favour of inclusion. John on the 34.99-hour case: 'why not include them? I'm a big fan of giving the auditors things to throw out.' Two-decimal half-up rounding stands, paired with a manual override so a reviewer can move an employee either way.
resolved_on_2026_08_20_call.missing_source_pay_periods: Confirmed by John unprompted: 'there is a missing pay period in this data, and that does happen to us.' He also confirmed the asymmetry we measured - 'it'll hurt you significantly on the min-max, but not on the pay period.'
